facts.text: Milford was originally part of Sunkhaze Plantation and incorporated in 1833, named for its valuable water power.
Milford’s landmark is the Milford Dam on the Penobscot River, a hydroelectric facility built in 1906 and listed on the National Register.
In the 20th century Milford shifted to energy production with the Milford Power Station built in 1921 to supply electricity for regional rail and hydro operations.
The climate of Milford swings sharply between warm summers and cold winters, a classic continental pattern for northern Maine.
Milford sits across the Penobscot River from Old Town, a neighboring community sharing the river’s scenic views.
The Sunkhaze Meadows National Wildlife Refuge lies within Milford, offering birdwatchers a chance to see migratory species along the Penobscot.
